name: Tom L Forest

bio.statement: The Capital Chronicle guide says Forest is a software engineer who previously worked for Nike, Intel and Portland General Electric.
bio.excerpt: Tom Forest is a software engineer who previously worked for Nike, Intel and Portland General Electric.

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Forest lists his occupation as software engineer, with a background at PGE, Thermofisher and Intel.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Software Engineer Occupational Background: Full-stack Software Engineer at PGE, Thermofisher, and Intel

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

bio.statement: Forest lists Hillsboro High School and a Bachelor of Science in management from MIT.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: Hillsboro High School; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Bachelor of Science, Management

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

bio.statement: Forest lists the Banks School District Budget Committee since 2012.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Banks School District Budget Committee, since 2012

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Forest says he will work to protect Oregonians from federal overreach such as ICE, vote-by-mail suppression and tax breaks for the rich.
positions.excerpt: I will work to protect us from Federal overreach like ICE, vote-by-mail suppression, and tax breaks for the rich.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Forest says he is opposed to bills that raise utility rates and give tax breaks to data centers and big tech in North Plains.
positions.excerpt: raise utility rates and give hundreds of millions of dollars in tax breaks for data centers and big tech in North Plains (SB1586). I'm a big "No" to all that.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Forest says he will focus on more jobs, fully funded education and rural transportation.
positions.excerpt: for more jobs, for fully funded education, for rural transportation

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Forest says communities can balance agricultural and natural resource economies with new industries.
positions.excerpt: There's room for both here, not letting the perfect be the enemy of the better.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 52

positions.statement: Forest's campaign website proposes disconnecting Oregon's tax code from the federal code and selectively reconnecting.
positions.excerpt: Let’s completely disconnect Oregon’s tax code from the federal code and selectively reconnect.

positions.statement: Forest's campaign website lists getting corporate money out of politics as an issue.
positions.excerpt: Get Corporate Money out of Politics

gaps: No policy positions: did not respond to the Capital Chronicle questionnaire
